items.bold: OVERNIGHT ESCALATION: US STRUCK QESHM ISLAND — Iran retaliated at Kuwait Airport. 1 INDIAN NATIONAL KILLED, 63 INJURED. Kuwait expelled 2 Iranian diplomats. Iran stopped mediator contact.
items.text: Washington Post, CBC News, Al Jazeera, Euronews (June 3-4): The US and Iran traded their most intense strikes since the April ceasefire began. CENTCOM struck an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz after Iran attacked a Botswana-flagged oil tanker heading toward Iran in defiance of the US blockade. Iran's IRGC immediately responded with 13 ballistic missiles and 17 drones targeting Kuwait and Bahrain. Kuwait Airport Terminal 1 was directly hit — 1 person killed (confirmed Indian national by India's Embassy in Kuwait and MEA), 63 injured including serious head wounds, amputations, and blast injuries. Kuwait's Defence Ministry destroyed over a dozen missiles and drones. Kuwait expelled 2 Iranian diplomats and issued a protest note. Kuwait Airways flights resumed at an alternate terminal. Iran's Foreign Ministry said Kuwait and Bahrain bore 'direct and clear responsibility' for allowing their territory to be used in US operations. Iranian media reported Iran had stopped communicating with ceasefire mediators following the Qeshm strikes. India's MEA condemned the attack: 'We condemn the attack on Kuwait International Airport today in which an Indian national has died and several of our nationals are injured.' India is now a direct casualty nation in this conflict for the second time (earlier: desalination facility, March 30).

items.bold: HOUSE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION PASSED 215-208 — bipartisan rebuke of Trump's Iran war. 4 Republicans joined Democrats. Symbolic but historic first passage.
items.text: NPR, Washington Post, CBC, ABC News (June 3): The US House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution 215-208 to halt Trump's military action against Iran — the clearest Congressional rebuke of the conflict since it began. Four Republicans (Massie, Fitzpatrick, Barrett, Davidson) joined all Democrats. The resolution is symbolic — it is a concurrent resolution that does not require the President's signature and heads to the Senate. Speaker Mike Johnson defended Trump's decision to attack Iran. The resolution had been delayed from two weeks earlier when Republican leaders sent members home early for May recess when it appeared the measure had enough votes. The passage signals growing bipartisan congressional pressure on Trump to end the war, which has lasted over 96 days and caused significant economic fallout. Trump acknowledged the war powers vote but maintained optimism about talks.

items.bold: TRUMP: Deal could happen 'over the weekend.' Iran 'pretty close.' Talks 'going very well.' BUT Iran stopped communicating with mediators. US now demanding WRITTEN nuclear commitments.
items.text: ABC News, Trading Economics (June 3): Despite the Qeshm/Kuwait escalation, Trump expressed optimism about the deal timeline. 'I hear the negotiation itself is going very well, actually. Very well,' Trump said. 'If it happens, it could happen, like, over the weekend.' Trump claimed Iran agreed not to pursue nuclear weapons. He also said he would be willing to meet Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Trump characterized the ceasefire situation: 'I'd say that part of the world, ceasefire is when you're shooting in a more moderate manner.' However: (1) Iranian state-linked news agencies reported Iran stopped communicating with mediators following Qeshm strikes. (2) The US is now seeking WRITTEN commitments from Iran on nuclear-related concessions — Iran had only provided verbal assurances. (3) The gap between Trump's optimistic public statements and the ground reality (escalating strikes, Iran halting mediation) is the defining tension of Day 96.

items.bold: CEASEFIRE STATUS: 'INCREASINGLY TENUOUS' (CBC/WaPo). Iran halted mediator contact. US seeks written nuclear commitments. Kuwait expelled Iranian diplomats. Hezbollah-Israel clashes escalating.
items.text: CBC News, Washington Post, Euronews (June 3-4): Multiple signals indicate the ceasefire is at its most fragile point since April 7. Iran stopped communicating with mediators after Qeshm strikes — the channel through which the ceasefire framework was maintained is now severed, at least temporarily. Kuwait expelled 2 Iranian diplomats — diplomatic downgrade of an Arab Gulf state is a structural obstacle to a regional settlement. US CENTCOM struck Iranian military infrastructure at Qeshm — strategically, this is an attack on Iran's Hormuz monitoring capability. Iran's Khamenei adviser warned of 'deluge of missiles' if US attacks continue. Hezbollah-Israel: Israeli strikes bombarded southern Lebanon overnight, Hezbollah claims 2 Israeli tanks destroyed. The multi-front nature of the conflict — Iran-US at sea, Iran-Kuwait-Bahrain in the Gulf, Hezbollah-Israel on land — makes any single ceasefire framework inadequate. For India: PGSA applications urgent, MEA contingency for Indian nationals in Gulf states now a critical priority.

military.t: US STRUCK QESHM ISLAND — Iran Retaliated at Kuwait Airport + Bahrain. 1 Indian National Killed. Kuwait Expelled 2 Iranian Diplomats. Iran Halted Mediator Contact.
military.d: Washington Post, Al Jazeera, CBC, Euronews (June 3-4): The most intense exchange of fire since the April ceasefire. Chain of events: (1) Iran attacked a Botswana-flagged oil tanker heading toward Iran despite the US blockade. (2) CENTCOM struck an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz entrance in 'self-defence.' (3) Iran's IRGC retaliated with 13 ballistic missiles and 17 drones targeting Kuwait and Bahrain. CENTCOM denied bases were hit. (4) Kuwait Airport Terminal 1 was struck, killing 1 Indian national (confirmed by India's Embassy and MEA) and injuring 63 others, including serious head wounds, amputations, and explosion injuries. (5) Kuwait expelled 2 Iranian diplomats. (6) Iranian state media reported Iran stopped communicating with ceasefire mediators. (7) Iran's FM declared Kuwait and Bahrain bore 'direct and clear responsibility.' (8) Khamenei adviser warned of 'deluge of missiles' if US attacks continue. Strategic significance of Qeshm strike: CENTCOM targeted Iran's Hormuz monitoring capability — Qeshm Island overlooks the Strait and hosts radar and coastal defence systems.

military.t: HOUSE WAR POWERS RESOLUTION 215-208 — Historic First Passage. 4 Republicans Join Democrats. Symbolic Rebuke of Trump's Iran War Powers.
military.d: NPR, Washington Post, ABC News (June 3): The US House passed the Iran war powers resolution 215-208 — the first time since the conflict began over 96 days ago. Four Republicans (Thomas Massie, Brian Fitzpatrick, Tom Barrett, Warren Davidson) joined all Democrats. The resolution is a concurrent resolution — symbolic, does not require President's signature, heads to Senate. Speaker Mike Johnson defended Trump's decision to attack Iran. Trump acknowledged the vote. Signals: (1) Bipartisan congressional fatigue with the 96-day conflict. (2) Growing economic pressure — inflation, oil prices, $25-50B war cost. (3) Political warning to Trump that continued escalation faces legislative resistance. The timing — same day as Qeshm/Kuwait escalation — creates contradictory signals: military escalation and legislative de-escalation pressure simultaneously.

assessment.body:
Thursday 9:30 AM IST. Day 96. The most dangerous 24 hours since the April ceasefire.

QESHM-KUWAIT ESCALATION
US struck Qeshm Island military ground control station near Hormuz.
Iran retaliated: 13 ballistic missiles + 17 drones at Kuwait + Bahrain.
Kuwait Airport Terminal 1 hit — 1 Indian national killed, 63 injured.
Kuwait expelled 2 Iranian diplomats.
Iran stopped communicating with ceasefire mediators.
This is the most significant military exchange since the April 7 ceasefire.

BRENT $96.89 — THREE STRAIGHT SESSIONS OF GAINS
From $91.89 Friday to $96.89 Wednesday — a $5/barrel rise in 3 days.
US crude inventories: sixth consecutive weekly drawdown of 6.8M barrels.
For India at Brent $97: OMC losses Rs 12-15/L petrol (post-second hike).
Diesel under-recovery Rs 28-32/L. Third hike timeline accelerated.

NIFTY 23,355 — MARKET VERDICT
Business Standard (live 9:30AM): Nifty 23,355 (-0.22%), Sensex 74,219 (-0.17%).
IT, Realty, Private Bank lagging. MidCap and SmallCap also lower.
Markets are absorbing two signals simultaneously:
(a) Escalation signal: Qeshm + Kuwait + Iran halts mediators = deal further delayed.
(b) Trump optimism signal: 'over the weekend' = deal still possible.
The market verdict: cautious decline, not panic. Support: 23,200-23,300.

HOUSE WAR POWERS 215-208
Historic first passage — bipartisan rebuke of Trump's Iran war.
4 Republicans joined Democrats. Symbolic but politically significant.
Senate consideration next. Not reaching Trump's desk as concurrent resolution.
Signal: Congressional pressure for deal will intensify.

THE VERDICT: Day 96 at 9:30 AM presents the sharpest contradiction of the war:
Trump optimism ('over the weekend') vs Iran halting mediators.
Qeshm military escalation vs House war powers constraint.
Brent $97 rising vs Trump's 'deal soon' signal.
The ceasefire is 'increasingly tenuous' — but both sides are still talking.
For India: one national killed, Nifty lower, Brent rising, third hike approaching.
When (if) the deal comes: Brent falls, Nifty surges, rupee stabilises.
Until then: India manages dual exposure — market risk + civilian safety risk.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
